description: Protocol/Evidence Advisor knowledge base — 6 evidence-backed rules (P1-P6). Each rule has citation DOIs. Descriptive only: match scores are not prescriptive.

rules.title: SYBR + high family cross-reactivity
rules.recommendation: SYBR Green cannot discriminate family members differing by 1 nt in the 3′ overhang region. Consider TaqMan probe-based detection, or design separate stem-loop RT primers for each family member.
pros: TaqMan eliminates non-specific signal
Separate RT primers give single-member specificity
cons: TaqMan probes add cost
Multiple RT reactions increase workload

sources.note: let-7 panel; members differ by 1 nt; SYBR required stringent annealing optimisation
original stem-loop RT-qPCR; specificity derives from stem-loop steric hindrance, not probe

rules.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate experimentally before use in any diagnostic context.

rules.title: Difficult sample type or low input RNA
rules.recommendation: Consider LNA-enhanced primers: literature reports improved accuracy and reproducibility at low RNA input (FFPE, plasma) compared to standard DNA primers.
pros: Improved Tm and hybridisation affinity for short miRNA targets [Andreasen10]
Reliable down to ~20 copies per reaction [Kunwar23]
Suitable for degraded RNA (FFPE, plasma)
cons: LNA oligo synthesis cost is higher than standard DNA
Require empirical Tm optimisation
Limited to research use without clinical validation

sources.note: LNA-enhanced primer improved quantification in total RNA from clinical samples
stem-loop TaqMan vs LNA-qPCR; both reliable to ~20 copies; LNA friendlier for clinical labs

rules.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate experimentally before use in any diagnostic context.

rules.title: SYBR Green detection (any assay)
rules.recommendation: Melting-curve analysis is mandatory with SYBR Green. Non-specific signal (primer-dimer, off-target) only becomes apparent in the melting curve and is not detectable from Cq alone.
pros: Detects primer-dimer and non-specific amplification products
Low cost — no probe required
cons: Adds analysis step
Cannot multiplex (single fluorescence channel)

sources.note: even LNA assays produced non-specific signal only revealed by melting curve

rules.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate experimentally before use in any diagnostic context.

rules.title: Multiplex or multi-target panel
rules.recommendation: For multiplex panels, consult stem-loop multiplex RT + dual-probe TaqMan literature. Primer cross-reactivity and probe spectral overlap must be verified empirically.
pros: Saves sample volume
Reduces cost and instrument time per target
Enables simultaneous normaliser co-amplification
cons: Primer/probe design complexity increases
May require optimisation of each primer pair concentration
Risk of competitive inhibition at high multiplex levels

sources.note: 21-miRNA multiplex stem-loop assay; cross-reactivity verification critical

rules.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate experimentally before use in any diagnostic context.

rules.title: Short or low-GC miRNA (edge E1 or E4)
rules.recommendation: For short (<18 nt) or low-GC (<30%) miRNAs, consider LNA substitution at 2-3 positions in the specific region, or extending the 5′ tail to raise forward primer Tm. Validate melting curve to confirm single-product amplification.
pros: LNA increases Tm by ~2-8°C per substitution for short targets [Andreasen10]
5′ tail extension achieves Tm without changing binding specificity
cons: LNA positions require empirical optimisation
Extended tails may increase primer-dimer risk — check structure_checks

sources.note: LNA spike for low-Tm miRNA targets
reliability at low copy number and difficult targets

rules.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate experimentally before use in any diagnostic context.

rules.title: Clinical or diagnostic application
rules.recommendation: For clinical laboratory applications, LNA-qPCR may offer operational advantages (CAP/CLIA compatibility, kit-based workflow). Both stem-loop TaqMan and LNA-qPCR are analytically comparable at >20 copies per reaction.
pros: LNA-qPCR demonstrated CAP/CLIA-compatible workflow [Kunwar23]
Stem-loop TaqMan well-established; extensive published validation [Chen05]
cons: Regulatory validation (IVD) requires additional clinical studies beyond analytical performance
This tool is for research use only

sources.note: analytical validation of CogniMIR miRNA panel; LNA-qPCR clinically friendlier

rules.disclaimer: For research use only. NOT validated for clinical in-vitro diagnostic (IVD) use. Requires independent clinical validation.

rules.title: Multi-target normalization (reference gene selection)
rules.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels
Global-mean assumes majority of miRNAs are unchanged — may not hold in disease states
Reference miRNA stability should be validated in your sample cohort before use

sources.note: geNorm normalization strategy for miRNA qPCR
Selecting 3 most stable miRNAs by multiple algorithms for normalization
Reference miRNA selection depends on sample type

rules.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.

rules.title: Circulating miRNA (plasma/serum) — preanalytical QC + spike-in
rules.recommendation: For circulating miRNA in biofluids: (1) add cel-miR-39-3p spike-in before RNA extraction to correct for variable extraction efficiency; (2) assess hemolysis (miR-16/miR-451a ratio, McDonald 2011); (3) use EDTA tubes and process within 2 h to minimize hemolysis-driven miRNA contamination. Hemolysis can introduce erythrocyte miRNAs (miR-92a, miR-451a) at >10-fold, masking true biofluid expression.
pros: cel-miR-39-3p spike-in corrects extraction efficiency variation and RT inhibition [Tan15]
Hemolysis check (miR-16/451a ratio) protects against erythrocyte miRNA contamination [McDonald11]
EDTA tubes reduce hemolysis vs. serum — use when study design permits
cons: Spike-in must be added before lysis/extraction, not after — incorrect timing invalidates normalization
Does not correct for differences in total RNA input — use synthetic miRNA ladder for input normalization
Hemolysis assessment adds one extra qPCR reaction per sample

sources.note: Spike-in normalization for serum/plasma miRNA; cel-miR-39 as exogenous control
Hemolysis alters plasma miRNA profile — miR-451a/miR-16 ratio as hemolysis marker
Anticoagulant tube type (EDTA vs serum) affects circulating miRNA yield and profile
